# PageLayout

PageLayout: the template for a full page, wrapping its content in the Frame with the Sidebar and the breadcrumb row.

Also asked as: page template, page shell.

**Import:** `import { PageLayout } from '@/patterns';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/patterns/PageLayout/PageLayout.jsx`

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/patterns/PageLayout/PageLayout.mdx`

## Usage

Start every page from a template. Pick the frame by the kind of work the page holds.

| Frame | When to use |
| --- | --- |
| Default | The person moves among pages: browse, compare, come back. It keeps the sidebar and the breadcrumb. |
| Focused | One task that takes more than a screen or a few minutes, which the person finishes or leaves. Writing a session note, setting up a session and reviewing an import are focused tasks. |

A confirmation, a rename or a few fields that keep the page behind them in view belong in a Modal; a form that scrolls for long or has sections is a focused page. The details of a row or a set of filters open in a Drawer over the template.

- **No top bar.** The sidebar and the page run the full height and meet at the sidebar's 1px edge.
- **No seams.** The page runs to the window edges. There is no frame pad around it.
- **Content cap.** 1232. With the sidebar docked it binds from a 1520 screen, and past that the margins grow. Narrower than 720, the page scrolls sideways.
- **The mode is the screen.** Medium is 768 to 1023, Large 1024 to 1439 and X-Large 1440 and wider. Sections, Cards and Tables inherit it and never carry one of their own.

### Build a real page

A page is built from the top down out of patterns. A Sessions page is built on Page, holding a page header, a row of metric cards and a table under a header with tabs.

1. **Frame.** The sidebar and the content box around the page.
2. **Section header, level page.** The page title, description and page-level actions. One per page.
3. **Card, size sm.** Metric tiles. A card shows one piece of information, with the header turned off when the body carries its own title.
4. **Section header, tabs type.** The tabs are the header's bottom row. They replace a separate tab group above the table.
5. **Table.** A plain table directly under the header, with no card around it and no toolbar of its own.

### For developers

The template is `PageLayout`, which fills `Frame` with the PLUS sidebar and the breadcrumb. `frame="focused"` fills it with the reading page, whose header row carries Back and Close, and the actions at its foot. There is no mode prop in code: the layout tokens switch on the viewport width, so the screen picks the mode. A page that needs the reading cap in the default frame composes `Frame` with `width="reading"`. Figma's `drawer?` toggle is the `drawer` prop: pass it the props of `PatternDrawer` and the template renders the Drawer over the page. Figma's `footer?` is `actions`: without them there are no actions at the foot. `contentDirect` puts the children straight in the page with no content grid, for a full-width page such as chat.

### The patterns

A pattern is a page-level shell with its layout rules built in. It sets the fill, radius, padding, elevation and width for one layer of the page, and leaves the content to slots. A page starts from a template. Frame holds the sidebar beside the Page, Page pads the content and gives it the 12-column grid, and Sections, Cards and Tables fill it. Overlays and Popups sit above the page.

In Figma the layout mode (Medium 768, Large 1024 or X-Large 1440) is a variable mode, set once on the template. In code the tokens follow the viewport width.

| Pattern | What it is | Use it for | In code |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

### A pattern or a component

Use a pattern to build a layer of a page: the frame, a region, a container for one object, a table, or a layer above the page. A pattern gives you the layer, never the content inside it. For a finished piece of UI such as a button, a field or an avatar, use the component. A pattern holds components in its slots, and a component never rebuilds a pattern's frame.

### How a page layers

Each layer has one fill and one elevation. A state such as hover or selected is drawn over the fill, never in place of it.

| Layer | Fill | Elevation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Frame | `--ds-surface-sunken` | none |
| Page | `--ds-surface` | none; an edge ring in `--ds-border-surface` |
| Section | none; the page shows through | none |
| Card | `--ds-surface-raised` | `--ds-shadow-raised`, no border |
| Table | none; its container owns the fill | none |
| Floating sidebar, Modal | `--ds-surface-overlay` | `--ds-shadow-overlay` |

Patterns nest by layer, and each layer's tokens belong to it. A Section holds a Card, and the Card holds the object's content. A Table is never wrapped in a Card.

## Best practices

### Start from the template and fill its slots. {#start-from-the-template-and-fill-its-slots}

A slot is a region left open for real content. The pattern owns the layout, the spacing and the size, and the slot holds what the feature needs.

Do: Start from the template and fill its slots.
Don't: Rebuild the page chrome by hand.

### Keep the slot wrapper. {#keep-the-slot-wrapper}

Replace the placeholder inside a slot, not the slot. If a layout is duplicated to handle a variation, that layout needs a slot. Slots live in Card (header, body, footer), Modal (body, footer), Section (content, side, actions, tabs) and the templates (the page). A table is never a slot shell.

Do: Keep the card attached. The content goes in the body slot, and the card’s own stack sets the spacing.
Don't: A card rebuilt by hand with 24 of extra space added to the chrome drifts from the pattern and misses later fixes.

### Pick the mode, never a width between modes. {#pick-the-mode-never-a-width-between-modes}

In Figma, pick Medium, Large or X-Large on the template instance, and never resize it to a width between modes. In code the screen picks the mode, so set nothing.

### Use the focused frame for a single task. {#use-the-focused-frame-for-a-single-task}

Do: Use frame=focused for a single task: Back, Close and its name, and nothing else competing.
Don't: Keep the sidebar on a one-task page, and its toggle and breadcrumb invite the person away.

If Back and Close would go to the same place, keep Close only.

### End-align the actions, one primary, last. {#end-align-the-actions-one-primary-last}

Do: End-align the actions at the foot, one primary, last.
Don't: Several primary actions, start-aligned: the person cannot tell which one finishes the task.

### Let the content pick the size. {#let-the-content-pick-the-size}

Choose the smallest step of a sized pattern (Card, Modal, Drawer) that holds the content without clipping. Never pick a size to make the content look a certain way.

### No card in a card, no modal over a modal. {#no-card-in-a-card-no-modal-over-a-modal}

A Card never holds a Card: group related cards in a Section instead. A Modal never opens a second Modal: a follow-up decision swaps the same Modal's content for an inline confirmation.

### Draw states as overlays. {#draw-states-as-overlays}

Hover, pressed and selected take their own token steps: `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered` and `-pressed`, then `--ds-background-selected` and `-hovered`. Focus is the focus ring in `--ds-border-focused`, never a fill.

### Keep filled versions as local components. {#keep-filled-versions-as-local-components}

A spec that fills Frame keeps its own component built from the pattern, so usage traces back to the pattern.

### Note every optical nudge. {#note-every-optical-nudge}

Spacing tokens set the structure. Where the eye needs a nudge, such as an icon beside text, an all-caps label or a round shape, nudge for optical balance and note it where you make it. Never leave it as an unexplained hard-coded value.

## Accessibility

- **Landmarks.** The sidebar's `nav` is the navigation and the page is the one `main`. The focused actions are a group named Page actions, or `actionsLabel`.
- **One page title.** The page has one `h1`. In the default frame it is visually hidden and the breadcrumb shows the place. In the focused frame it is the visible title in the Page header row.
- **Focus order.** In the focused frame it is Back, Close, the content, then the actions. In the default frame the sidebar toggle comes first, then the page.
- **Names.** Back and Close are icon buttons named Back and Close (`backLabel`, `closeLabel`), and Close keeps its name when the title truncates.
- **Sidebar.** The toggle reports whether the sidebar is open. Hover is never the only way in: the toggle opens and docks it from the keyboard, and Escape closes a floating sidebar.
- **Drawer.** It is a dialog named by its title. It moves focus inside, keeps Tab there and returns focus to its trigger.
- **Color.** The frame, the page and the title use color roles, so they hold their contrast in Light, Dark and increased contrast.

## Parts

The default frame has three parts.

1. **Frame.** The sidebar beside the page, on the sunken fill.
2. **Header.** The page's first row, 32 high on the sidebar logo row's center line: the breadcrumb. While the sidebar is closed the toggle leads it. Help Center and the account sit in the sidebar's account row.
3. **Content.** A slot in the page. It holds a page-level Section header and the Sections. The page's `h1` is `title`, visually hidden.

The focused frame has three parts, all in the Frame with no sidebar.

1. **Header row.** 32 high, held at the top of the Page while it scrolls. Back, an icon button with `arrow-left`, leads; the title, the page's one visible `h1` at Heading/xsmall on one line that truncates, follows; Close, an icon button with `xmark`, ends the row. Each button is drawn only with its handler.
2. **Content.** The Page's `main` at reading width: Sections capped at 864, centered and never under 720. It scrolls on its own.
3. **Actions** (optional). A group inside the Page, held at its foot while it scrolls, end-aligned in the content column, 8 apart, the primary action last. Without `actions` there is none.

The page carries the content grid, 12 columns with a 16 gutter. The screen grid lives on Blanket only, and the modal guide belongs to Modal.

### States

A template has no interactive states of its own. The sidebar's docked, collapsed, peeking and overlay states are the Frame's; the shell can also load (`shellLoading` shows the breadcrumb as a skeleton) and enter (`shellEntered` plays the header and sidebar entrance).

### Tokens

The layout mode is the screen width: **Medium** is 768 to 1023, **Large** is 1024 to 1439 and **X-Large** is 1440 and wider. Every value below moves with the mode.

#### Screen

| Token | Medium | Large | X-Large | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--screen-width` | 768 | 1024 | 1440 | The width of the template frame. |
| `--screen-pad-x` | 24 | 24 | 32 | Pads the screen grid on Blanket, not the page grid. |
| `--screen-min-width` | 768 | 1024 | 1440 | The narrowest the frame goes within the mode. |
| `--screen-max-width` | 1023 | 1439 | none | The widest the frame goes within the mode. X-Large has no limit. |

#### Grid

| Token | Medium | Large | X-Large | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--grid-columns` | 12 | 12 | 12 | The column count at every width. |
| `--grid-gutter` | 16 | 16 | 16 | The gap between columns, in every grid. |
| `--grid-width-column` | 45.33 | 46.67 | 81.33 | One column of the content grid. |
| `--grid-width-column-screen` | 45.33 | 66.67 | 88 | One column of the screen grid. |

#### Content

| Token | Medium | Large | X-Large | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--content-max-width` | 1232 | 1232 | 1232 | The content cap. |
| `--content-max-width-reading` | 864 | 864 | 864 | The reading cap. |
| `--content-min-width` | 720 | 720 | 720 | Narrower than this, the page scrolls sideways. |
| `--content-width` | 720 | 736 | 1152 | The content width at 768, 1024 and 1440. It reaches 1232 from a 1520 screen. |

#### Frame

| Token | Value | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--frame-sidebar-width` | 240 | The sidebar, docked from 1024. |
| `--page-pad` | 24 | The page pad at every width. The grid margin is the same token. |
| `--page-radius` | 8 | The Page's corner radius token. The Frame places the Page flush, so it does not apply it. |

#### Focused page

| Token | Value | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--focused-page-stack-sm` | 8 | Above and below the actions at the foot of the Page. |
| `--focused-page-inline-sm` | 8 | Between the actions. |
| `--content-max-width-reading` · `--content-min-width` | 864 · 720 | The content column and the actions column. |
| `--ds-surface` · `--ds-text` | color | The header row and the actions bar, and the title. They follow Light, Dark and increased contrast. |

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name a focused task in its title: "Add a session note". | The app area: "Sessions". |
| Show the place in the breadcrumb: "Home / Sessions". | A visible page title that repeats the breadcrumb. |
| Put only Sections in a focused page. | A sidebar, a card grid or a table toolbar beside them. |
